long_desc:
This report is designed as a "framework" in a way that it is easy to add new KPIs as needed.  
A unique feature is how it incorporates "Month to Date" logic meaning you can run it in the current month.   If you run it on the 18th of Sept, it compares it to where you were on the 18th of Aug.
This gives it much better accuracy when comparing month-over-month, especially for array stats.
EXAMPLE:
Say from Aug 1 to Aug 31 your  thin pool usage went from 400TB to 800TB, roughly 10 TB per week
If I want to compare this month to last month and today is the 18th you are only looking at 18 days, so you will be comparing 18 days worth vs 30 days worth so the report will way off.
What this logic does (automagically) is, it knows today is the 18th so it only chooses the first 18 days of last month instead of all 31 days of last month.  Tomorrow it will be 19, etc.
 
The only other alternative is to compare whole months which would mean you could never run the report for the current month.
i.e. if I ran it in Sept, I could only look at July and Aug.

long_desc:
Long Description: 
This report accepts a date range and performs a Period-Over-Period(POP) analysis based on that date range.  If you select last 7 days, it will compute values and compare to prior 7 days, if you select last 30 days it will compare to prior 30 days, etc.  The report will first compute the data, then present an analysis of the results.  There is a delta value which represents the POP change in both volume and as a percentage.  It then breaks down the delta into several metrics, the sum of those will equal the delta.  The metrics include:
New Clients - Clients backed this period but did not exist in the prior period
Retired Clients - Clients that backed up in the prior period but are not in the current period
Clients who decreased - Clients whose total backup volume decreased compared to the prior period.
Clients who increased... 
Between 1% to 20%
Between 20% to 50%
Between 50% to 100%
Over 100%
problem_stmt:
I can see that my backup job volume increased over the past 30 days but I need to explain why.

long_desc:
This report is designed as a "framework" in a way that it is easy to add new KPIs as needed.  
A unique feature is how it incorporates "Month to Date" logic meaning you can run it in the current month.  If you run it on the 18th of Sept, it compares it to where you were on the 18th of Aug.
This gives it much better accuracy when comparing month-over-month, especially for backups stats.
EXAMPLE:
Say from Aug 1 to Aug 31 you did 40,000 backup jobs, roughly 10,000 jobs per week
If I want to compare this month to last month and today is the 18th you are only looking at 18 days, so you will be comparing 18 days worth vs 30 days worth so the report will way off.
What this logic does (automagically) is, it knows today is the 18th so it only chooses the first 18 days of last month instead of all 31 days of last month.  Tomorrow it will be 19, etc.
 
The only other alternative is to compare whole months which would mean you could never run the report for the current month.
i.e. if I ran it in Sept, I could only look at July and Aug.
problem_stmt: I need high level KPI's on my backup environment that I can present to my CIO, i.e. more information, less data.

long_desc:
Determining whether a client was successful or not is complicated.  Especially if there are multiple policies and schedules defined for that client and if there are multiple streams per backup set.  Also there needs to be an established cutoff time to determine what to do if a client is still running or has not made all if its attempts.
Here is what the report determines:
1. If a client fails all of its jobs it is failed.
2. If a client successfully completes all of its jobs it is successful.
3. If a client completes all of its jobs with status 1 (skipped files) it was partially successful and probably OK.
4. If a client has a mixture of successful jobs and failed jobs, we need to look into whether they were truly successful or not.  
Now, there is logic that can be applied to #4 in order to programmatically determine whether a client was successful or not but that logic varies from customer to customer.

The report predicts the availability of media based on the expiration date of the media. Using this report, you can determine what media will be available for reuse. The stacked bar chart represents the number of media of a specific type that are expired or going to expire on a particular day. Different colors are used for different media types in the stacked bar chart. Mouseover for the bar segments provide the media type and count of the media that is available on that day. Run this report by selecting future start and end date range from the scope selector.
Users can drilldown from the bar for a specific date to obtain complete details about the Tape Media such as the barcode, serial number, Used KB etc.

Note: For drilldown report ' NetBackup Media Expiration Schedule Detail ' to work some manual steps need to be followed:
  1) First, Import the drilldown report ' NetBackup Media Expiration Schedule Detail. Execute the report by selecting any date in scope. It should produce empty output.
   (Note: DO NOT Import the main report ' NetBackup Media Expiration Schedule’ yet. We will do that later.)

     b. replace all occurrences of 100522 with the "SQL Template ID" numeric value you saved earlier (Note: When you import a report a new ID is allocated) and save the file.
  4) Now, import the main report ' NetBackup Media Expiration Schedule ' into your environment. 
  5) Run the Main report ' NetBackup Media Expiration Schedule ' by selecting future start and end date from the scope selector. If there are Tape media expiring on days that fall in that date range  you will see a stacked bar chart with unique color for each Tape Media Type. Click on the Bar to drilldown to see

long_desc:
This report is designed as a "framework" in a way that it is easy to add new KPIs as needed.  
A unique feature is how it incorporates "Month to Date" logic meaning you can run it in the current month.   If you run it on the 18th of Sept, it compares it to where you were on the 18th of Aug.
This gives it much better accuracy when comparing month-over-month, especially for SAN stats.
EXAMPLE:
Say from Aug 1 to Aug 31 you added 40 ports, roughly 10 ports per week
If I want to compare this month to last month and today is the 18th you are only looking at 18 days, so you will be comparing 18 days worth vs 30 days worth so the report will way off.
What this logic does (automagically) is, it knows today is the 18th so it only chooses the first 18 days of last month instead of all 31 days of last month.  Tomorrow it will be 19, etc.
 
The only other alternative is to compare whole months which would mean you could never run the report for the current month.
i.e. if I ran it in Sept, I could only look at July and Aug.
problem_stmt: I need high level KPI's on my SAN environment that I can present to my CIO, i.e. more information, less data.

long_desc:
This report is designed as a "framework" in a way that it is easy to add new KPIs as needed.  
A unique feature is how it incorporates "Month to Date" logic meaning you can run it in the current month.   If you run it on the 18th of Sept, it compares it to where you were on the 18th of Aug.
This gives it much better accuracy when comparing month-over-month, especially for VM stats.
EXAMPLE:
Say from Aug 1 to Aug 31 you added 40 new VM guests, roughly 10 per week
If I want to compare this month to last month and today is the 18th you are only looking at 18 days, so you will be comparing 18 days worth vs 30 days worth so the report will way off.
What this logic does (automagically) is, it knows today is the 18th so it only chooses the first 18 days of last month instead of all 31 days of last month.  Tomorrow it will be 19, etc.
 
The only other alternative is to compare whole months which would mean you could never run the report for the current month.
i.e. if I ran it in Sept, I could only look at July and Aug.
